name: Google libaddressinput (countryinfo.txt)
note: Postal metadata for roughly 240 countries: the regular expression a postcode must
match, and the layout an address is written in. Apache-2.0, which is the licence this
The address format is the part with no other source. `%N%n%O%n%A%n%C %S %Z` says a US
address puts name, organisation and street on their own lines and then city, state and
ZIP on one -- and `〒%Z%n%S%C%n%A%n%O%n%N` says a Japanese one runs the other way
entirely, postcode first and name last. That is exactly what `location.postal_address`
encodes, and faker carried it for twelve locales as hand-written strings.
Pinned to a commit: the file changes when a country reforms its postcodes, which should
be a deliberate re-pin rather than a silent change in what every address looks like.
